Twenty comments

This is a tune I’ve known for a long time, having picked up a version from the CD, The Poet & The Piper, played by Liam O’Flynn. Poems by Seamus Heaney and much played a few years ago by Ciaran MacMathuna on the radio, Mo Cheoil Thu.
I was trying to remember how it started there the other night and looking here for a few notes, was surprised to see it’s not listed.
There’s also a version credited to O’Neill’s on the web as follows:
D|G2(cB)G(B A)FA|G2(c B)GB c2d|ege dc(B A)FD|E2c- ccA G2D|G2(c B)G(B A)FA|G2(c B)GB c2d|ege dc(B A)FD|E2(c B)cA G2||
||d|gdB gd(B- A)FD|(gf)(e d)ef g2d|ege dc(B A)FD|E2(c B)cA G2d|gdB gd(B A)FD|(gf)(e d)ef g2d|ege dc(B A)FD E2(c B)cA G2|]

Re: Open the Door for Three

Here’s a clip of Liz Knowles and Kieran O’Hare playing Open the Door for Three, with a minor third part:

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pYskj9BPlEo

The tune starts at 2:44 and the third part comes in at 3:37. They play the tune AABBAABBCCAABBCC.

The sleeve notes to the album Open the Door for Three (by Knowles, O’Hare, and Pat Broaders) likely explains where they found the third part.

And here’s the track from the album, with the same format for the tune as the live clip above (tune starts at 3:20).
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9jPuLccpLXs
